clue.text: Recording everything produced by pop act, high or tripping

indicators.note: tripping suggests someone high on drugs, so these letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A pop band, stoned and hallucinating, produce some sort of recording.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tripping' scrambles POP ACT HIGH OR; 'produced by' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A photographic memory is one that retains every detail, as if taking a picture of it.

clue.text: Set up rapper to get busted with drug

indicators.note: busted means broken, so the letters of the word rapper are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: E is the slang abbreviation for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A rapper is framed by being arrested in possession of drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set up' looks like a frame-up but is the plain definition; 'to get busted' rearranges RAPPER.
explanation.definitionFit: To prepare something is to get it ready, i.e. arrange or establish it in advance.

clue.text: Cause of tears when knife is wielded, with unusual number arrested getting conviction

indicators.note: arrested means held or captured, so one piece is held inside the other

parts.words: Cause of tears when knife is wielded
parts.note: chopping an onion makes the eyes water
pi is an unusual, irrational number

explanation.surface: A knife attack, a strange numerical clue and an arrest lead to a criminal conviction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrested' and 'conviction' suggest a court case, but conviction here is a firm belief.
explanation.definitionFit: A firmly held belief or view can be called a conviction.

clue.text: More than one living being made from India following keyboard text service

indicators.note: following means the letter for India comes after the instrument

parts.note: an organ is a keyboard instrument
I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet
SMS is the short message service for phone texts

explanation.surface: Something is assembled from an Indian keyboard and a texting service.
explanation.definitionFit: Organisms are living creatures; the plural fits 'more than one'.

clue.text: Traitors, retaining European judges

indicators.note: retaining means holding on to, so the letter sits inside the other word

parts.note: rats are informers or turncoats

explanation.surface: Turncoats are holding on to a European official.
explanation.definitionFit: To rate something is to assess or appraise it, a verb sense matching 'judges'.

clue.text: Tommy's secret

definitions.meaning: Tommy (Atkins) is slang for a British army soldier, the lowest rank

explanation.walkthrough: Tommy is the traditional nickname for a British private soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: A Tommy is a common soldier of the lowest rank; secret means confidential.

clue.text: Had round in time to meet journalist after six

indicators.note: after means the time-and-journalist pair follows the numeral

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals
ED is short for editor

explanation.surface: Someone arrives promptly to meet a reporter just after six o'clock.
explanation.definitionFit: To have someone round is to invite them to your home.

clue.text: Crime series creates results

parts.note: a con is a swindle, a crime
sequences are series of things in order

explanation.surface: A crime drama series produces outcomes.
explanation.definitionFit: Consequences are outcomes that follow from actions.

clue.text: Scribbling heartlessly after love split

indicators.note: after means the trimmed writing word follows the zero

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

indicators.note: heartlessly means one of the central letters is removed

parts.note: scribbling is writing, penning

explanation.surface: Someone writes cold-heartedly after a break-up with a lover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartlessly' drops one of the two middle Ns of PENNING, leaving PENING.
explanation.definitionFit: A split is a gap or opening, a crack in something.

clue.text: They steal this, having cased day before

indicators.note: cased means enclosed in a case, so the word this wraps round the day

parts.note: an eve is the day before an event

explanation.surface: Burglars steal this item, having cased the joint the day before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cased' looks like burglars' slang for scouting a place; here it means encasing.
explanation.definitionFit: Thieves are people who steal, so the phrase describes them.

clue.text: Grisly pun Sir Dicky makes in a funny way

indicators.note: dicky is British slang for unsound or shaky, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A knight named Dicky makes a gruesome pun that is oddly amusing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dicky' looks like a name for Sir but is the anagram signal for GRISLY PUN SIR.
explanation.definitionFit: Funny can mean strange or unexpected, so doing something unexpectedly is doing it in a funny way.

clue.text: BBC or Channel 5, say? Lad consumes rubbish one

indicators.note: consumes means eats up, so the boy's word swallows the other pieces

parts.note: a son is a lad
tat is cheap rubbish
I is one in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A boy watches a trashy programme on British TV.
explanation.walkthrough: BBC and Channel 5 are British broadcasters; the question mark marks them as examples.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadcaster such as the BBC or Channel 5 is a TV station, an example rather than a synonym.

clue.text: Break shower switching taps?

indicators.note: taps are marked C and H, cold and hot, so cold is switched for hot

parts.note: to shower is to scatter, as with confetti

explanation.surface: A broken shower needs its taps swapped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'switching taps' replaces C (cold) in SCATTER with H (hot).
explanation.definitionFit: To shatter is to break into pieces.

clue.text: In essence, mystique enfolds her

indicators.note: in essence means at the core, so the letters are found inside the words

explanation.surface: A woman is wrapped in an air of mystery.
explanation.definitionFit: Her Majesty is the monarch's title, so 'her' stands for a female sovereign.

clue.text: Give up on French — translate

parts.note: sur is French for on
to render a text is to translate it

explanation.surface: Someone abandons a translation from French.
explanation.definitionFit: To give up is to yield or capitulate.

clue.text: On offensive, not in at the beginning or ending

parts.note: RE means on or concerning

indicators.note: not says the following letters are missing
at the beginning says where the removed letters were, at the front of the word

parts.note: insulting means offensive
taken as written

explanation.surface: On the attack, joining neither at the start nor at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not ... at the beginning' strips the opening letters; 'or' is only a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A thing resulting in another is ending in it, as an outcome.

clue.text: Cuts out about 13 physical jerks

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the cutting word goes round the royal letters

parts.note: excises means cuts out
13 across is QUEEN, abbreviated ER (Elizabeth Regina)

explanation.surface: Someone cuts out about thirteen gym exercises.
explanation.walkthrough: 13 points to the answer at 13 across; ER stands for a queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Physical jerks is a British term for keep-fit workouts or callisthenics.

clue.text: Like Tibet and Nepal, banning anything odd, authoritarian

indicators.note: banning the odd letters keeps only the even-placed ones of the word Nepal

parts.note: stern means strict, authoritarian

explanation.surface: Tibet and Nepal are imagined as strict states that ban anything unusual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tibet and Nepal' looks like the definition, but Nepal is wordplay: its even letters give EA.
explanation.definitionFit: Tibet lies in Asia, in the East, so it is an oriental place.

clue.text: Pluck our nestling in aviary?

indicators.note: nestling in means settling snugly inside, so the word our sits inside the bird enclosure

parts.note: an aviary is a large bird cage

explanation.surface: We pluck a baby bird from its aviary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pluck' and 'nestling' suggest birds, but pluck is the definition and nestling is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Pluck means bravery or nerve.

clue.text: Inputs marks

definitions.meaning: keys text in at a keyboard
models or kinds, as in Mark II, sorts

explanation.definitionFit: Inputting text is keying it in; marks are kinds or sorts.

clue.text: Worry no one's bag will turn up

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means reading from the bottom upwards

parts.note: one is I, and 's stands for is, giving IS
to net is to bag or catch

explanation.surface: No one should fret that their lost bag will reappear.
explanation.definitionFit: Tension is anxiety or nervous strain.

clue.text: Abbreviation — abbreviation of 17, to be exact

parts.note: a precis is a summary or abridgement
17 down is Eastern, abbreviated E

explanation.surface: A shortened form is presented as the exact one.
explanation.definitionFit: Precise means exact or accurate, an adjective matching 'to be exact'.

clue.text: Outfit uniform this person's found beyond price

indicators.note: beyond means coming after, so the letters follow the price word

parts.note: cost is price
U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet
this person is the setter, me

explanation.surface: The setter finds a uniform too expensive.
explanation.definitionFit: A costume is a set of clothes, an outfit.

clue.text: Moderate undermined by Left — that holds up work

indicators.note: in a down clue being undermined means having something placed beneath

parts.note: to ease is to moderate or lessen

explanation.surface: A political moderate is sabotaged by the Left, which holds up legislation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holds up work' suggests delay; it is a stand that supports a painting.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist's stand supports a canvas being painted.

clue.text: Idea that's a non-starter — seabird that carries a light!

indicators.note: a non-starter loses its first letter

parts.note: a plan is an idea or scheme
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A hopeless idea: a seabird carrying a lamp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'non-starter' looks like 'hopeless idea' but drops the first letter of PLAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A lamp in a case carries a flame or bulb, a portable light.

clue.text: Notice cutter's sails repeatedly up and down

parts.note: to see is to notice
a cutter is a saw, and 's stands for is or has, giving SAWS

explanation.surface: Someone notices a cutter, a small boat, sailing up and down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutter' suggests a boat but is a saw.
explanation.definitionFit: To seesaw is to move back and forth or up and down alternately.

clue.text: Original sign

definitions.meaning: to mark a document with one's first letters

explanation.definitionFit: Initial means first or original; to initial a document is to sign it with initials.

clue.text: Restlessly lie in — neglect to give reason

indicators.note: restlessly suggests tossing and turning, so these letters are moved around

explanation.surface: Lying in bed fitfully and neglecting your duties to give a reason.
explanation.definitionFit: Reason is the power of thought, a synonym of mental capacity or brains.
